clue.text: Arrangement for Tuesday, about noon? It's not firmly fixed

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the piece for noon
an arrangement of the word Tuesday puts its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Tuesday meeting around midday is booked, and is told it is still provisional.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark dresses a scheduling query; 'Arrangement for' is the anagram signal, with 'about' wrapping the scramble round noon's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wobbly or insecure is not firmly fixed in place, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Snobbish at Oxford or Cambridge? Cause for regret

parts.note: a student in residence at Oxford or Cambridge is said to be up
a pity is something to be regretted, as in 'what a pity'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Oxbridge snobbery is a thing to be sorry about.
explanation.walkthrough: Being UP means in residence at a university, traditionally Oxford or Cambridge; you 'go up' at the start of term.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppity describes someone arrogantly self-important, which matches snobbish behaviour closely.

clue.text: Since overthrown, retreat is most rational

indicators.note: overthrown in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'
a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: A government toppled, someone retreats to the most sensible course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' turns AS upside down to SA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The sanest person is the one with the soundest mind, hence the most rational.

clue.text: Delighted to find the fourth door?

parts.note: a door is an entrance to a building
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet, used to label a fourth door

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled to locate the fourth doorway at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Doors are often labelled A, B, C, D, so the fourth door is ENTRANCE D.
explanation.definitionFit: Entranced means held spellbound with wonder, a strong form of being delighted.

clue.text: Piece of music, composition of Verdi with tempo not varying

indicators.note: a composition puts things together, so the letters of these words are assembled afresh

parts.note: tempo in music is the time, as in 'keep time'

indicators.note: varying means the letters of not are also shifted about

explanation.surface: A musical piece by Verdi is described as having a steady tempo throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition of' mixes VERDI, TIME (tempo) and NOT, the last also 'varying', into the twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A divertimento is a light instrumental work, typically for a small ensemble, so a piece of music.

clue.text: Saying British retreated in rear

indicators.note: retreated means the whole sequence goes backwards

parts.note: a motto is a short saying

explanation.surface: A remark about the British falling back at the rear of a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreated' turns MOTTO + B round to B-OTTOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom is the backside, so rear in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Smoothly running band I conducted

parts.note: a band or ring is round in shape like the letter O
to conduct is to lead, past tense led

explanation.surface: A bandleader says the group was in fine form under their direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a group of musicians beside 'conducted', but it is a ring, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that has been lubricated runs smoothly, so oiled means running without friction.

clue.text: Writer interrupting sailor, one found in pub

indicators.note: interrupting means one word breaks into the middle of another

parts.note: tar is a traditional word for a sailor
Jules Verne, the French author of science fiction

explanation.surface: A novelist barges in on a sailor drinking at the local.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverner keeps or frequents a tavern, so is a person you would meet in a pub.

clue.text: With young lady, hide having character faults?

parts.note: Miss is the title for a young unmarried woman
pell is an old word for a skin or hide

explanation.surface: A young woman concealing her moral failings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character faults' reads as flaws of personality, but characters here are letters: to misspell is to write letters wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the letters of a word wrong is to make faults with written characters.

clue.text: Joke I have about it is intended to teach a lesson

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the word it

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: A comic insists his wordplay has an instructive purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Punitive measures are punishments meant to deter, i.e. to teach a lesson.

clue.text: Lots of garlic and spices

definitions.meaning: the segments of a garlic bulb, several of them
dried flower buds used as a fragrant spice

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the separable segments of a garlic bulb and the aromatic dried buds of the clove tree.

clue.text: Hits bad drive — nevertheless, securing par, ultimately survives

parts.note: in golf, to pull a drive is to hit it off line to the left

indicators.note: securing means holding something inside, as one word grips another

parts.note: though can mean nevertheless, as in 'it rained, though'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of par

explanation.surface: A golfer slices a tee shot but still makes par and comes through the round.
explanation.walkthrough: Golfers say a shot is pulled when it hooks off line; the golf surface also makes 'par' look like a score rather than a word to take a letter from.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull through is to recover from illness or difficulty, an idiom for surviving.

clue.text: Tragic opera Sardou created, acted originally

definitions.text: Tragic opera Sardou created, acted originally

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A note that the French playwright Sardou wrote the drama behind a famous tragic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Puccini's opera was based on Victorien Sardou's play La Tosca, so the whole clue both defines and spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera, ending in the heroine's leap from a castle, is a celebrated tragic opera from Sardou's play.

clue.text: Journey that gets you back home about fall

definitions.text: Journey that gets you back home

parts.note: round can mean about, as in 'round the house'
to trip is to stumble or fall

explanation.surface: A journey home that involves taking a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey out and back again to the starting point, the opposite of a one-way trip.

clue.text: Vulnerable part of a cold fish embracing female

parts.note: a chill is a cold, the illness

indicators.note: embracing means holding the female pronoun within the fish

parts.note: an eel is a fish
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A fish's weak spot is said to be a cold one hugging a female.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero's only weak spot was his heel, so the phrase names any weak point.

clue.text: Least affected because on holiday

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: since can mean because
a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: Someone is the least pretentious because they are away on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The most sincere person is the one with the least affectation or pretence.

clue.text: Old newspapers merged frequently

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
The Times, the British newspaper

explanation.surface: Old newspapers frequently combined in mergers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newspapers' supplies two papers: the FT (Financial Times) and THE TIMES, Britain's daily, joined ('merged').
explanation.definitionFit: Ofttimes is an archaic word meaning often, i.e. frequently.

clue.text: Drink ensnaring another new and inexperienced person

indicators.note: ensnaring means holding other pieces trapped inside

parts.note: beer is a drink
another drink, gin

explanation.surface: A drink trap catches another newcomer who is inexperienced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' carries on from 'Drink' and means a second drink, which is why it gives a spirit rather than a general word.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner is a novice just starting out, so lacking experience.

clue.text: International author going around checking in situ

indicators.note: going around means the author's name wraps round the other piece

parts.note: Henry Fielding, the English novelist who wrote Tom Jones
an international is a sporting contest between countries, a meet

explanation.surface: A globetrotting writer travels about checking things on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A field meeting is an outdoor gathering held on location, hence checking things on the spot.

clue.text: Couple engaged in silly chat

parts.note: at can mean engaged in, as in 'at work'

indicators.note: silly means the letters of chat are muddled

explanation.surface: A pair caught up in idle gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' is the anagram signal for the word chat, and 'engaged in' supplies a short preposition, as in being busy at a task.
explanation.definitionFit: To couple things is to join or fasten them together, which is to attach.

clue.text: Help struggling actor in concert part

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: Someone helps a nervous performer during a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous London summer series of concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompter feeds a forgotten line to an actor, which is to prompt.

clue.text: Cheat thrown out of Patrick's territory

indicators.note: the answer is cast out from within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A swindler is expelled from Patrick's land.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickster is one who deceives people, so a cheat.

clue.text: Capital having moved to another city in same country

indicators.note: having moved means a run of letters is shifted to a different place in the word

parts.note: Tokyo is the capital of Japan

explanation.surface: A capital relocated to another Japanese city.
explanation.walkthrough: Kyoto was the imperial capital of Japan before Tokyo, so the surface is historically true; 'to' in the clue names the very letters that are moved.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto is another major city in Japan, the same country as Tokyo.

clue.text: Go into American centre without a cent

indicators.note: without means the coin's letter is removed

parts.note: center is the American spelling of centre
C is the abbreviation for cent

explanation.surface: Someone goes into a US shopping centre with no money.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go into a place.

clue.text: No term off for this teacher

indicators.note: off means the letters are disturbed or rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher who never gets any time off during term.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is a trusted adviser who guides and teaches.

clue.text: Not having high temperature, with doctor fighting onset of malaria

parts.note: St Luke the evangelist was a physician
war is fighting

indicators.note: onset of means the first letter of malaria

explanation.surface: A doctor in a war zone reports that a malaria case has no fever yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm means only tepid, so not hot.

clue.text: Special norms about European minister's speech

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the European piece
special means the letters of norms are reshaped into a special order

explanation.surface: Particular standards are set out regarding Europe in a minister's address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Special' is the anagram signal for norms, giving SRMON, and 'about' wraps that round European's letter.

clue.text: Gossip of spiteful woman about problem

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful woman
